test a per-horizon weighted scheme using softmax_neg_error on the full pool to see if horizon‑specific weighting helps with unstable ranking and trend dominance.
test a weighted combination that uses inverse_error on the full pool to see if simple error weighting beats the robust mean, exploiting the strong trend but unstable ranking.
test a trimmed mean over the full pool to see if removing extreme outliers improves the robust mean, given the trend-dominated, high predictability series.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a robust median may reduce influence of outliers and extreme errors.
Test a per‑pool weighted combination using softmax_neg_error on the stable pool4 to see if limiting to the top 8 models improves over full‑pool softmax.
test robust DBA over all models
test forward‑selection weight over full pool
The series has an unstable ranking and strong trend; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting on the stable subset pool4 may capture subtle horizon changes while remaining robust.
The ranking is unstable and the series is trend‑dominated; a robust DBA on the stable subset pool4 may outperform the simple mean.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 1.0. Series context: trend strength 0.9601 and seasonal strength 0.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.228); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 6.983.
